title: A Human-Factors Guided Cognitive Model of Visuospatial Complexity in Embodied Active Vision
comment: Preprint; AIC 2025: Artificial Intelligence and Cognition
summary: We propose a novel framework for the analysis of multimodal data -- encompassing visual, auditory, and spatial stimuli -- foregrounding the role of complexity in embodied perception and interaction in dynamic, naturalistic settings. Grounded in theories of embodied cognition and active vision, we argue that embodied perceptual complexity emerges from an agent's dynamic engagement with the environment and must be analyzed holistically, as a combination of qualitative and quantitative attributes pertaining to, for instance, visuospatial and auditory features. Building on previous work on visual complexity, we expand this into a categorization of diverse complexity attributes -- quantitative, structural, dynamic, auditory, and interactional -- that together characterize multimodal complexity. We demonstrate how this model provides a theoretical framework for characterizing aspects of visuospatial complexity and their interactions, specifically in the context of everyday driving. We also discuss practical applications of the proposed model for creating and evaluating benchmark datasets (e.g., in driving) that centralize cognitive human factors, as well as applications aimed at systematically investigating the effect of visuospatial complexity on human active vision from the viewpoint of visual perception research. The proposed framework lays the foundation for automated methods that interpret complexity in 3D dynamic environments from a human-centered perspective, serving as a semantic template for explainable computational analysis of visuospatial complexity with a categorical focus on cognitive human factors.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a novel theoretical framework for analyzing multimodal complexity in embodied perception, expanding visual complexity into five categories (quantitative, structural, dynamic, auditory, and interactional) and demonstrating applications in driving scenarios and benchmark dataset design.
AI.motivation: Existing approaches to complexity in perception are fragmented and focus primarily on visual stimuli in isolation, failing to account for the holistic, multimodal nature of embodied perception in dynamic, naturalistic environments such as driving.
AI.method: The framework builds on prior work on visual complexity and expands it into a categorization of five complexity attributes—quantitative, structural, dynamic, auditory, and interactional—grounded in embodied cognition and active vision theories, which together characterize multimodal complexity.
AI.result: The model is demonstrated as a theoretical framework for characterizing visuospatial complexity and its interactions in everyday driving, with practical applications for creating/evaluating benchmark datasets and investigating effects on human active vision.
AI.conclusion: The framework lays the foundation for automated, explainable computational analysis of visuospatial complexity in 3D dynamic environments, serving as a semantic template centered on cognitive human factors.

title: InfoDPP-PAC: Principled Patch Selection for Whole Slide Image Analysis
summary: Each WSI slide contains thousands of candidate tissue patches, while supervision is usually available only at slide level. Existing bag-construction strategies like Uniform extraction and handcrafted heuristics do not control redundancy while attention-based multiple-instance models couple patch importance to a particular downstream classifier, and coreset methods optimise embedding-space coverage without modelling task-relevant patch quality. We introduce InfoDPP-PAC, a principled patch-selection framework that combines teacher-seeded Gaussian process relevance modelling, determinantal log-determinant diversity,submodular greedy optimisation, and a concentration-based adaptive stopping rule. The main theoretical result shows that the log-determinant diversity term used in DPP-style selection is the Gaussian process mutual information between a selected subset and the latent relevance function. We further derive a PAC-style certificate for residual information gain, allowing the number of retained patches to vary by slide rather than being fixed a priori. The empirical study evaluates whether the selected subset is diverse, spatially and morphologically covering, non-redundant, and enriched for the teacher-derived relevance signal. It does not claim end-to-end diagnostic improvement after retraining a downstream MIL model. On 202 HISTAI gastrointestinal whole-slide images, the adaptive rule uses 83.7% fewer patches on average than a fixed full budget while retaining 97.9% of full-budget composite selection quality. At a matched budget, InfoDPP-PAC achieves the highest mean teacher-derived relevance score among fourteen baselines, with diversity and composite scores close to the strongest coreset methods. The results support InfoDPP-PAC as a controlled quality-diversity-cardinality selection framework, rather than as a downstream clinical predictor.

AI.tldr: InfoDPP-PAC is a principled patch-selection framework for whole-slide images that combines Gaussian process relevance modelling, determinantal diversity, submodular greedy optimisation, and an adaptive stopping rule. It reduces patch usage by 83.7% while retaining 97.9% of full-budget selection quality on 202 gastrointestinal WSIs, and achieves the highest teacher-derived relevance score among fourteen baselines at a matched budget.
AI.motivation: Existing bag-construction strategies for WSI analysis either fail to control redundancy (Uniform extraction, handcrafted heuristics), couple patch importance to a specific downstream classifier (attention-based MIL), or optimise only embedding-space coverage without task-relevant quality (coreset methods). A principled selection framework that simultaneously models patch quality, diversity, and cardinality is needed.
AI.method: InfoDPP-PAC combines four components: (1) teacher-seeded Gaussian process relevance modelling for patch quality, (2) determinantal log-determinant diversity for non-redundancy, (3) submodular greedy optimisation, and (4) a concentration-based adaptive stopping rule. Theoretically, it proves the log-determinant diversity term equals the GP mutual information between the selected subset and the latent relevance function, and derives a PAC-style certificate for residual information gain allowing slide-varying cardinality.
AI.result: On 202 HISTAI gastrointestinal WSIs, the adaptive rule uses 83.7% fewer patches on average than a fixed full budget while retaining 97.9% of full-budget composite selection quality. At a matched budget, InfoDPP-PAC achieves the highest mean teacher-derived relevance score among fourteen baselines, with diversity and composite scores close to the strongest coreset methods.
AI.conclusion: InfoDPP-PAC is positioned as a controlled quality-diversity-cardinality patch selection framework rather than a downstream clinical predictor. It does not claim end-to-end diagnostic improvement after retraining a downstream MIL model, but demonstrates principled selection with strong quality, diversity, and efficiency properties.

title: A nonlinear dynamics approach to assess amplitude-frequency coupling in non-invasive human electrogastrography recordings
summary: Conventional electrogastrography (EGG) analyses summarize gastric slow-wave activity using dominant frequency, power, or phase-based metrics, without explicitly modeling amplitude-dependent frequency dynamics. We developed a statistical nonlinear-dynamics framework that represents the gastric-band analytic EGG signal as a stochastic Stuart-Landau oscillator and estimate local effective phase-shear, $β_{\mathrm{eff}}$, a normalized measure of amplitude-frequency coupling. In overnight recordings from 60 healthy participants, effective phase-shear was consistently negative, generalized to held-out halves of each recording, and was abolished by amplitude surrogates that disrupted amplitude-phase alignment while preserving amplitude-series structure. We then applied the measure to fasted and fed recordings from 16 healthy participants and 24 participants with gastric dysfunction. Phase-shear magnitude differed between groups and classified dysfunction comparable to the strongest multielectrode phase-based traveling-wave measures. These findings establish amplitude-frequency coupling as a dynamical feature of gastric-band EGG that complements conventional spectral and spatial phase metrics, while motivating future multichannel observation models to determine its relationship to slow-wave propagation and gastric function.

AI.tldr: The paper develops a statistical nonlinear-dynamics framework that models gastric-band EGG signals as a stochastic Stuart-Landau oscillator to estimate local effective phase-shear (β_eff), a normalized measure of amplitude-frequency coupling. Applied to healthy participants and those with gastric dysfunction, the measure is robust, reproducible, differs between groups, and classifies dysfunction comparably to multielectrode phase-based traveling-wave measures.
AI.motivation: Conventional EGG analyses rely on dominant frequency, power, or phase-based metrics that do not explicitly model amplitude-dependent frequency dynamics. The authors aim to establish amplitude-frequency coupling as a complementary dynamical feature of gastric slow-wave activity.
AI.method: The authors model the gastric-band analytic EGG signal as a stochastic Stuart-Landau oscillator and estimate a normalized measure of amplitude-frequency coupling called local effective phase-shear (β_eff). They validate it with held-out data and amplitude surrogates, then apply it to fasted/fed recordings from healthy participants and those with gastric dysfunction.
AI.result: Effective phase-shear was consistently negative in 60 healthy participants, generalized to held-out halves of recordings, and was abolished by amplitude surrogates. Phase-shear magnitude differed between healthy and dysfunctional groups and classified gastric dysfunction comparably to the strongest multielectrode phase-based traveling-wave measures.
AI.conclusion: Amplitude-frequency coupling is a genuine dynamical feature of gastric-band EGG that complements conventional spectral and spatial phase metrics. Future work should develop multichannel observation models to determine its relationship to slow-wave propagation and gastric function.

title: Optimizing RNA yield using deep neural networks coupled to massively parallel screening
summary: Messenger RNA (mRNA)-based therapeutics have emerged as a powerful platform for vaccines, protein replacement therapies, and cancer immunotherapy. A critical bottleneck in mRNA development is manufacturing large quantities of RNA economically, as measured by RNA yield emerging from an in vitro transcription (IVT) reaction. However, how promoter-adjacent DNA sequences influence RNA yield remains poorly characterized. Here, we present an integrated deep learning framework that leverages massively parallel next-generation sequencing (NGS) assays to measure RNA yield across large sequence spaces. A library of 10^5 randomized oligonucleotide sequences was designed to systematically explore sequence diversity within a defined structural context. DNA and RNA abundances were quantified in parallel using Illumina sequencing, enabling high-resolution measurement of sequence-to-yield relationships at scale. Sequences were one-hot encoded and used to train deep learning models, using a convolutional neural network architecture. The model achieved a Pearson correlation of 0.94 between predicted and experimentally measured RNA yield on a held-out test set, demonstrating strong generalization across diverse sequence contexts. Importantly, the trained model can be deployed in a production environment to score and rank novel RNA sequence designs by predicted IVT yield, enabling cost-effective, pre-experimental prioritization of the most manufacturable candidates. This framework establishes a scalable, data-driven approach to DNA and RNA sequence optimization, with broad applicability to vaccine antigen design, therapeutic protein delivery, and synthetic biology. By integrating high-throughput experimentation with advanced deep learning modeling, it significantly reduces screening costs and accelerates RNA engineering cycle times.

AI.tldr: This paper presents an integrated deep learning framework that uses massively parallel NGS assays to measure and predict RNA yield from in vitro transcription (IVT) across large sequence spaces, achieving a Pearson correlation of 0.94 on held-out test data and enabling pre-experimental prioritization of manufacturable RNA sequence designs.
AI.motivation: mRNA therapeutics are powerful but face a critical bottleneck in manufacturing RNA economically. The influence of promoter-adjacent DNA sequences on RNA yield is poorly characterized, creating a need for scalable, data-driven approaches to predict and optimize RNA manufacturability.
AI.method: A library of 10^5 randomized oligonucleotide sequences was designed to explore sequence diversity within a defined structural context. DNA and RNA abundances were quantified in parallel via Illumina sequencing. Sequences were one-hot encoded and used to train a convolutional neural network (CNN) to predict RNA yield from sequence.
AI.result: The CNN model achieved a Pearson correlation of 0.94 between predicted and experimentally measured RNA yield on a held-out test set, demonstrating strong generalization across diverse sequence contexts. The model can be deployed in production to score and rank novel RNA sequences by predicted IVT yield.
AI.conclusion: This framework establishes a scalable, data-driven approach to DNA and RNA sequence optimization with broad applicability to vaccine antigen design, therapeutic protein delivery, and synthetic biology, significantly reducing screening costs and accelerating RNA engineering cycle times.

title: Finch: Toxicity Dose Response Curve Prediction of Chemical Compounds and Mixtures
summary: A holistic approach to chemical mixtures is reshaping risk assessment emphasizing mixture testing over single compounds eliminating animal testing and advancing modeling methods. Most computational models still focus on individual chemicals and conventional mixture models like concentration addition and independent action are limited they struggle with multiple Modes of Action and often miss synergistic or antagonistic effects. Regulatory agencies need faster more efficient models that go beyond these constraints. Finch addresses these challenges with a novel workflow. It integrates molecular descriptor based frameworks and deep learning embeddings in multi task quantitative structure activity relationship models for improved chemical exposure prediction. DL embeddings preserve information from diverse inputs molecular descriptors physicochemical properties and large language model embeddings from SMILES by distilling key features into a latent space enhancing machine learning predictions. Finch multi task learning optimizes multiple loss functions simultaneously leveraging all available data to learn generalized representations. This enables effective modeling of complex ingredient interactions within mixtures offering a significant advancement for regulatory safety assessment.

AI.tldr: Finch is a novel computational workflow that integrates molecular descriptors, physicochemical properties, and large language model embeddings from SMILES into multi-task QSAR models to predict chemical exposure and model complex ingredient interactions in chemical mixtures, overcoming limitations of traditional mixture models like concentration addition and independent action.
AI.motivation: Regulatory agencies need faster, more efficient computational models for chemical mixture risk assessment. Conventional mixture models (concentration addition, independent action) are limited because they struggle with multiple Modes of Action and often miss synergistic or antagonistic effects. Most existing computational models still focus on individual chemicals rather than mixtures.
AI.method: Finch uses a multi-task quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) framework. It integrates molecular descriptor-based models with deep learning embeddings by distilling features from diverse inputs (molecular descriptors, physicochemical properties, and LLM embeddings from SMILES) into a latent space. Multi-task learning optimizes multiple loss functions simultaneously to learn generalized representations from all available data.
AI.result: The approach enables effective modeling of complex ingredient interactions within mixtures, offering improved chemical exposure prediction and a significant advancement for regulatory safety assessment beyond conventional mixture modeling limitations.
AI.conclusion: Finch represents a significant methodological advancement in chemical mixture risk assessment, moving beyond single-compound and conventional mixture models by leveraging deep learning and multi-task learning to capture complex mixture interactions while supporting animal-testing-free regulatory workflows.

title: Global geometry of the genotype-phenotype map illuminates a trade-off between penetrance and mutational adaptability
summary: Evolution in changing environments requires both reliable expression of the currently favored phenotype, as quantified by penetrance, and the capacity to reach alternative phenotypes through mutation. Previous studies suggest that high penetrance may restrict such mutational access. However, because these studies focus on evolved genotypes and local mutational neighborhoods, they cannot determine whether this local constraint limits mutational adaptability under environmental change. Such adaptability depends on a genotype's position relative to high-fitness regions for other environments. Addressing this question requires reconstructing the full probability distribution over phenotypes for every genotype and the resulting environment-specific fitness landscapes across genotype space. Such reconstruction is generally infeasible because genotype and phenotype spaces grow combinatorially. Here, an abstract model of stochastic genotype-phenotype mapping, inspired by interacting spins in statistical physics, permits exhaustive reconstruction of the map. We find that high-penetrance genotypes tend to occupy the interior of environment-specific high-fitness regions and are mutationally robust, whereas lower-penetrance genotypes tend to lie near their boundaries and have greater mutational access to high-fitness regions for alternative environments. This global geometry generates a trade-off between penetrance and mutational adaptability. In evolutionary simulations, stronger phenotypic noise in a fixed environment increases the selective advantage of reliable expression, thereby favoring high penetrance and mutational robustness. Frequent environmental change instead favors mutational accessibility at the expense of penetrance. Thus, penetrance and adaptability are opposing consequences of the same global geometry, with environmental conditions determining their evolutionary balance.

AI.tldr: This paper uses an abstract statistical physics-inspired model of genotype-phenotype mapping to exhaustively reconstruct fitness landscapes, revealing a global geometric trade-off between penetrance (reliable expression of the current phenotype) and mutational adaptability (access to alternative high-fitness phenotypes). High-penetrance genotypes occupy fitness-region interiors and are mutationally robust, while low-penetrance genotypes lie near boundaries with greater mutational access. Evolutionary simulations show environmental conditions determine the balance: stable environments favor penetrance, while frequent environmental change favors adaptability.
AI.motivation: Previous studies suggested high penetrance may restrict mutational access to alternative phenotypes, but because they focused only on evolved genotypes and local mutational neighborhoods, they could not determine whether this local constraint limits mutational adaptability under environmental change. Addressing this requires reconstructing the full probability distribution over phenotypes for every genotype and environment-specific fitness landscapes, which is generally infeasible due to combinatorial growth of genotype and phenotype spaces.
AI.method: The authors develop an abstract model of stochastic genotype-phenotype mapping inspired by interacting spins in statistical physics, which permits exhaustive reconstruction of the full map. They analyze the global geometry of high-fitness regions across genotype space, then run evolutionary simulations under different environmental conditions to test how phenotypic noise and environmental change rate affect the evolvability-penetrance balance.
AI.result: High-penetrance genotypes tend to occupy the interior of environment-specific high-fitness regions and are mutationally robust, whereas lower-penetrance genotypes tend to lie near boundaries with greater mutational access to high-fitness regions for alternative environments. Stronger phenotypic noise in a fixed environment favors high penetrance and mutational robustness, while frequent environmental change favors mutational accessibility at the expense of penetrance.
AI.conclusion: Penetrance and mutational adaptability are opposing consequences of the same global geometry of fitness landscapes, with environmental conditions determining their evolutionary balance. This provides a unified framework connecting phenotypic reliability, mutational robustness, and evolvability.

title: Primate vision reveals a missing principle for robust dynamic AI
summary: How does an intelligent visual system combine what objects look like with how they move while remaining robust as appearance changes? We addressed this question by comparing human perception and neural activity in macaque inferior temporal cortex with representations from image- and video-based neural networks spanning recognition, segmentation, optic-flow processing and predictive world modeling. Temporal integration improved object representations, but most video recognition models generalized poorly when appearance was disrupted while motion structure was preserved. Humans and macaque IT remained robust. Notably, predictive world models combined strong cross-appearance generalization with the closest correspondence to IT, outperforming other video-modeling approaches in neural fidelity. Yet no model reproduced the cortical transformation from early appearance-dominated responses toward later appearance-invariant motion coding. These results identify progressive integration of motion into object representations as a principle of robust dynamic vision and implicate predictive learning as a promising route toward realizing this computation in artificial systems.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how biological visual systems combine object appearance with motion information while maintaining robustness to appearance changes, comparing human perception and macaque IT cortex activity against various neural network models. Predictive world models best matched biological neural representations and cross-appearance generalization, though no model fully replicated the cortical progression from appearance-dominated to appearance-invariant motion coding.
AI.motivation: To understand how biological visual systems achieve robust dynamic vision by integrating object appearance and motion, and to determine which computational approaches most closely mirror the neural mechanisms underlying this capability.
AI.method: The authors compared human perceptual judgments and macaque inferior temporal cortex recordings against representations from multiple neural network architectures, spanning image-based (recognition, segmentation), video-based (optic-flow, predictive world models) approaches, testing both temporal integration benefits and cross-appearance generalization while preserving motion structure.
AI.result: Temporal integration improved object representations across models, but most video recognition models generalized poorly when appearance was disrupted. Humans and macaque IT remained robust. Predictive world models achieved the strongest cross-appearance generalization and the closest neural correspondence to IT, yet no model replicated the cortical transformation from early appearance-dominated toward later appearance-invariant motion coding.
AI.conclusion: Progressive integration of motion into object representations is a key principle of robust dynamic vision, and predictive learning represents a promising computational route toward achieving this in artificial vision systems, though current models fall short of fully capturing the cortical dynamics observed biologically.

title: Kernel-Dependent Pattern Formation in a Population Model with Nonlocal Facilitation and Competition
summary:
Spatial patterns, such as those in dryland vegetation models, have historically been studied
  in systems of reaction-diffusion systems with pattern onset via a Turing bifurcation from a spatially uniform state. More recently, spatial patterns have been considered in models that incorporate spatially extended interactions via nonlocal interaction kernels. It remains largely underexplored if and how the choice of nonlocal interaction kernel contributes to differences in pattern formation and persistence, particularly in models that contain competition and facilitation. Here, we investigate spatial patterns in a reaction-diffusion model for a single species that includes nonlocal competition and facilitation processes; Gaussian, exponential, algebraic, hat, and smooth hat kernels are considered as specific examples. Via a center manifold analysis, and using the relative spatial scale of competition to facilitation and the death rate as bifurcation parameters, we identify that the choice of kernel has impacts on the pattern forming bifurcation. Bifurcations using the Gaussian, exponential, and algebraic kernels largely follow expectations of Turing patterns, but patterns in the hat and smooth hat kernels can form even when the scale of competition is less than that of facilitation. The dynamics of patterns far from onset are investigated via numerical continuation methods. The model produces the so-called "Turing-before-Tipping" phenomenon demonstrating that the arrangement into spatial patterns is an effective resilience mechanism against harsh conditions. Again, there is a kernel-dependent dichotomy in pattern behavior. Early warning signs for population extinction are observed with the Gaussian, exponential, and algebraic kernels, but not under the hat or smooth hat cases.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes how different nonlocal interaction kernels (Gaussian, exponential, algebraic, hat, smooth hat) affect spatial pattern formation and persistence in a reaction-diffusion model with nonlocal competition and facilitation, revealing kernel-dependent bifurcation behavior and resilience mechanisms.
AI.motivation: While spatial patterns in dryland vegetation have been classically studied via Turing bifurcations in reaction-diffusion systems, it remains underexplored how the specific choice of nonlocal interaction kernel influences pattern formation and persistence in models with competition and facilitation.
AI.method: The authors analyze a single-species reaction-diffusion model with nonlocal competition and facilitation using five kernel types. They employ center manifold analysis with the relative competition-to-facilitation scale and death rate as bifurcation parameters, and use numerical continuation methods to study patterns far from onset.
AI.result: Kernel choice significantly impacts pattern-forming bifurcations: Gaussian, exponential, and algebraic kernels follow standard Turing pattern expectations, while hat and smooth hat kernels can form patterns even when competition scale is smaller than facilitation scale. The model exhibits 'Turing-before-Tipping,' showing pattern formation is a resilience mechanism against harsh conditions. Early warning signs for extinction appear with Gaussian, exponential, and algebraic kernels, but not with hat or smooth hat kernels.
AI.conclusion: The choice of nonlocal interaction kernel fundamentally alters pattern formation behavior and resilience signaling, revealing a kernel-dependent dichotomy in both bifurcation structure and extinction early warning capability.

title: Quantifying the Biophysical Properties of Red Blood Cells in Gaucher Disease
comment: 25 pages, 7 figures. Supporting Material included as an ancillary file
summary: Gaucher disease (GD), the most common lysosomal storage disorder, alters red blood cell (RBC) mechanics and circulation, contributing to vascular occlusions, bone infarcts, and splenomegaly. However, the individual roles of GD-RBC biophysical properties in these processes remain unclear. Here, we present a combined computational-experimental investigation to quantitatively characterize GD-RBC biophysical properties and determine how specific mechanical parameters drive abnormal RBC behavior. Informed by experimental data, we independently quantify key RBC properties, including shear modulus (mu), surface-to-volume ratio (S/V), and bending modulus (k_c). Based on these parameters, we construct three GD-RBC subtypes (GD-RBC1-3) to systematically isolate their individual contributions. At the single-cell level, optical tweezers simulations show up to ~27% reduction in axial diameter and ~42% reduction in transverse compression. Tank-treading dynamics exhibit non-monotonic behavior, with rotation frequencies increasing by up to ~70% or decreasing under elevated bending rigidity. In confined flow, traversal times through microchannel constrictions increase by more than a factor of two, while splenic slit passage times rise from ~250 ms (control) to >1200 ms for the severe GD-RBC subtype, approaching a functional no-passage threshold. At the population level, viscosity simulations demonstrate that these alterations collectively elevate blood viscosity, with small fractions (~4.0%) of highly rigid cells disproportionately increasing flow resistance. Overall, this study provides a quantitative and mechanistic framework that disentangles the contributions of key RBC parameters to abnormal behavior in GD, linking cellular-scale biophysics to hematologic dysfunction and microvascular occlusion.

AI.tldr: This study integrates computational simulations with experimental data to quantitatively characterize the biophysical properties of red blood cells (RBCs) in Gaucher disease (GD), isolating the individual contributions of shear modulus, surface-to-volume ratio, and bending modulus. It identifies how these parameters drive abnormal RBC behaviors—including reduced deformation, altered tank-treading dynamics, prolonged traversal through microchannels and splenic slits, and elevated blood viscosity—linking cellular mechanics to microvascular occlusion and hematologic dysfunction.
AI.motivation: Gaucher disease alters RBC mechanics and circulation, contributing to vascular occlusions, bone infarcts, and splenomegaly, but the individual roles of specific GD-RBC biophysical properties remain unclear.
AI.method: A combined computational-experimental approach: experimental data inform independent quantification of shear modulus, surface-to-volume ratio, and bending modulus; three GD-RBC subtypes are constructed to isolate individual parameter contributions; optical tweezers simulations, tank-treading dynamics analysis, confined flow and splenic slit transit simulations, and population-level blood viscosity simulations are performed.
AI.result: Up to ~27% reduction in axial diameter and ~42% reduction in transverse compression; tank-treading rotation frequencies change by up to ~70% (increase or decrease depending on bending rigidity); microchannel traversal times more than double; splenic slit passage times rise from ~250 ms to >1200 ms for severe subtypes; blood viscosity increases with only ~4.0% highly rigid cells disproportionately raising flow resistance.
AI.conclusion: This study provides a quantitative mechanistic framework disentangling the contributions of key RBC parameters to abnormal behavior in GD, linking cellular-scale biophysics to hematologic dysfunction and microvascular occlusion.

title: Beauty is in the ELBO of the Beholder: A Variational Account of Processing Fluency in Face Perception
summary: Facial attractiveness has been linked to statistical regularities such as symmetry and averageness, suggesting that beauty may depend on the ease with which a face is perceived. We empirically test this hypothesis by training variational autoencoders on four face datasets without attractiveness supervision and evaluating their representations on the 597 faces from the Chicago Face Database. Across models, human attractiveness ratings closely aligns with the direction defined by the VAE evidence lower bound (ELBO) in rate-distortion space. Independently learned latent spaces contain an attractiveness direction that transfers strongly across random initializations and training data. We also find that attractive faces are more prototypical in both shape and latent space. Our results connect classic accounts of aesthetics with learned generative models and provide empirical support for a variational interpretation of the processing fluency theory of aesthetic pleasure.

AI.tldr: The paper tests the hypothesis that facial attractiveness relates to ease of perception by training variational autoencoders on four face datasets without attractiveness labels. Human attractiveness ratings align with the VAE's ELBO in rate-distortion space, and attractive faces are more prototypical, supporting a variational interpretation of processing fluency theory.
AI.motivation: Facial attractiveness has been linked to statistical regularities (symmetry, averageness), suggesting beauty may depend on perceptual ease. The authors aim to empirically test this processing fluency hypothesis using learned generative models.
AI.method: Train variational autoencoders on four face datasets without attractiveness supervision. Evaluate their latent representations on 597 faces from the Chicago Face Database. Analyze the relationship between human attractiveness ratings and the VAE's ELBO in rate-distortion space, and examine attractiveness direction in latent spaces across random initializations and training data.
AI.result: Human attractiveness ratings align closely with the ELBO-defined direction in rate-distortion space across models. Attractiveness direction transfers strongly across random initializations and training data. Attractive faces are more prototypical in both shape and latent space.
AI.conclusion: The findings connect classic accounts of aesthetics with learned generative models and provide empirical support for a variational interpretation of the processing fluency theory of aesthetic pleasure.

title: Validation of HRV Studio: A Transparent and Quality-Control-Aware Platform for Heart Rate Variability Analysis
comment: 33 pages, 8 figures. Source code available at https://github.com/CyrusMexon/HRV-Analysis_TJU
summary: Reproducibility of heart rate variability (HRV) analysis is limited by differences in preprocessing and computational conventions across software platforms. We developed HRV Studio, an open-source PyQt6-based desktop application integrating transparent HRV analysis with automated quality-control (QC) diagnostics. Validation included large-scale agreement with NeuroKit2, targeted Kubios benchmarking, spectral-method comparison, synthetic perturbation testing, recording-duration sensitivity analysis, and arrhythmia-focused QC stress testing. HRV Studio showed near-identical agreement for the widely used time-domain indices RMSSD and SDNN under matched conditions. In the primary five-minute NeuroKit2 comparison, frequency-domain median relative errors were 1.35% for LF, 0.18% for HF, and 1.41% for LF/HF, while VLF remained more convention-sensitive (37.79%). Nonlinear Poincaré indices also demonstrated high consistency. Sequence-harmonized Kubios benchmarking confirmed near-identical agreement for time-domain and nonlinear indices and strong agreement for most frequency-domain measures. Extended ten-minute analyses reproduced the same overall pattern with lower disagreement for some convention-sensitive spectral outputs. Synthetic and arrhythmia stress tests maintained 100% numerical stability while consistently triggering QC warnings. Overall, HRV Studio provides a transparent and reproducible platform for HRV research, with strong cross-platform consistency when NN sequences, preprocessing, and analytical conventions are harmonized. Stress-test results indicate computational robustness rather than clinical validation.

AI.tldr: The authors developed HRV Studio, an open-source PyQt6-based desktop application for heart rate variability (HRV) analysis with transparent preprocessing and automated quality-control diagnostics. Extensive validation against NeuroKit2 and Kubios showed near-identical agreement for time-domain indices (RMSSD, SDNN) and nonlinear indices, with low frequency-domain errors (0.18-1.41%) except convention-sensitive VLF (37.79%). Stress tests confirmed 100% numerical stability with consistent QC warning triggers.
AI.motivation: HRV analysis reproducibility is limited by differences in preprocessing and computational conventions across different software platforms, creating a need for a transparent, standardized, and reproducible HRV analysis tool.
AI.method: Developed an open-source PyQt6-based desktop application (HRV Studio) integrating transparent HRV analysis with automated QC diagnostics. Validated through large-scale comparison with NeuroKit2, Kubios benchmarking, spectral-method comparison, synthetic perturbation testing, recording-duration sensitivity analysis, and arrhythmia-focused QC stress testing.
AI.result: Near-identical agreement for RMSSD and SDNN under matched conditions. Frequency-domain median relative errors of 1.35% (LF), 0.18% (HF), 1.41% (LF/HF) in five-minute comparisons, with VLF showing higher convention sensitivity (37.79%). Nonlinear Poincaré indices showed high consistency. Extended ten-minute analyses reproduced the same pattern. Stress tests maintained 100% numerical stability while triggering QC warnings appropriately.
AI.conclusion: HRV Studio provides a transparent and reproducible platform for HRV research with strong cross-platform consistency when NN sequences, preprocessing, and analytical conventions are harmonized. Stress-test results confirm computational robustness but should not be interpreted as clinical validation.

title: Evaluating Deep Multivariate Imputation Models on Wearable Device Data
summary: Wearable device data enables continuous health monitoring, but suffers from structured missingness: features sharing a physical sensor drop out together. Deep imputation methods such as BRITS and SAITS have seen limited evaluation on multimodal physiological data under realistic missingness, and existing benchmarks use random-point holdout protocols that incorrectly assume missingness is independent across features and time. Using data from a person with epilepsy recorded on a Garmin smartwatch, we develop an evaluation protocol that mines contiguous missing-run templates from training data, stratifies them by per-feature gap-length quantiles, and injects them as block masks with preserved co-missingness structure. A matched training protocol exposing models to the same missingness distribution reduces BRITS's severe-gap MAE by 43%, demonstrating the potential benefit of the proposed evaluation and training protocol within this single-participant dataset. We further extend BRITS with time-of-day encoding and a circadian harmonic channel. No single model dominates: linear interpolation is optimal for slow-moving features over short gaps; extended BRITS achieves lower MAE on dynamic cardiac features in moderate and severe gaps; and SAITS better preserves the ground-truth distribution by Jensen-Shannon distance despite higher MAE. Ultimately, model rankings strongly depend on evaluation designs. By exposing how traditional evaluation methods obscure true model capabilities, our transferable protocol establishes critical steps towards developing better imputation strategies for future multi-sensor wearable datasets.

AI.tldr: This paper addresses the problem of structured missingness in wearable device data, where features sharing a physical sensor drop out together. The authors develop a novel evaluation protocol that mines contiguous missing-run templates from training data and injects them as block masks preserving co-missingness structure, using data from a person with epilepsy on a Garmin smartwatch. They show that a matched training protocol reduces BRITS's severe-gap MAE by 43%, and demonstrate that no single imputation model dominates, with rankings strongly depending on evaluation designs.
AI.motivation: Deep imputation methods (BRITS, SAITS) have had limited evaluation on multimodal physiological data under realistic missingness patterns. Existing benchmarks use random-point holdout protocols that incorrectly assume missingness is independent across features and time, obscuring true model capabilities for real-world wearable data where physical sensors cause features to drop out together.
AI.method: The authors develop an evaluation protocol that: (1) mines contiguous missing-run templates from training data, (2) stratifies them by per-feature gap-length quantiles, and (3) injects them as block masks with preserved co-missingness structure. They also introduce a matched training protocol exposing models to the same missingness distribution. Additionally, they extend BRITS with time-of-day encoding and a circadian harmonic channel.
AI.result: The matched training protocol reduces BRITS's severe-gap MAE by 43%. No single model dominates: linear interpolation is optimal for slow-moving features over short gaps; extended BRITS achieves lower MAE on dynamic cardiac features in moderate and severe gaps; and SAITS better preserves ground-truth distribution by Jensen-Shannon distance despite higher MAE.
AI.conclusion: Model rankings strongly depend on evaluation designs. Traditional evaluation methods obscure true model capabilities, and the proposed transferable protocol establishes critical steps towards developing better imputation strategies for future multi-sensor wearable datasets.

title: Potential survivable niches for microbial life on the lunar south pole
comment: 43 pages, 3 figures, 3 tables, Preprint of Science Advances published on Aug. 19, 2026
summary: Most lunar surface conditions are incredibly harsh for microbial survival. High ultraviolet radiation, temperatures, and energetic particle radiation limit survival over most unprotected lunar surfaces, particularly in equatorial regions where all previous crewed exploration occurred. However, whether these harsh conditions are widespread at lunar poles has not been examined considering topographical effects. Here, we show that recent microorganism survivability data and lunar surface remote sensing reveal likely survivable niches in lunar polar regions. Analysis of topography and latitude-driven surface conditions using remote sensing data and high-resolution illumination models indicates the lunar south pole possesses significant regions with persistent low temperatures and ultraviolet flux. Comparing these conditions to survivability data of specific microorganisms, we find significant lunar polar areas likely possess surface conditions amenable to microbial survival. Our findings suggest lunar polar regions may be less hostile to microbial survival than previously assumed. This does not encompass growth likelihood, but survival in a cryptobiotic state where growth would be possible if habitable conditions were present. Potential microbial survivability at lunar poles is particularly significant given many examined microbes will likely be transported to the Moon during crewed lunar south pole exploration planned in numerous near-term missions. Thoughtfully planning exploration and tracking its impact is key to limiting and understanding potential unintended life transfer to the Moon.

AI.tldr: Recent microorganism survivability data combined with lunar surface remote sensing reveals that the lunar south pole contains significant regions with persistent low temperatures and low ultraviolet flux, creating likely survivable niches for microbes in a cryptobiotic state. This challenges assumptions that all unprotected lunar surfaces are lethal to microbial life and has implications for potential unintended biological contamination during upcoming crewed south pole missions.
AI.motivation: While equatorial lunar regions (where all previous crewed missions occurred) are known to be extremely harsh for microbial survival due to high UV radiation, temperatures, and energetic particles, whether these conditions are equally severe at lunar poles—especially considering topographical effects—has not been systematically examined. With near-term crewed missions planned for the lunar south pole, understanding potential microbial survivability is critical for contamination control and planetary protection.
AI.method: The authors integrate recent microorganism survivability data with lunar surface remote sensing data. They analyze topography and latitude-driven surface conditions using remote sensing data combined with high-resolution illumination models to assess persistent low temperatures and ultraviolet flux at the lunar south pole. These conditions are then compared against survivability thresholds for specific microorganisms.
AI.result: The analysis indicates the lunar south pole possesses significant regions with persistent low temperatures and reduced ultraviolet flux. Comparing these surface conditions to documented microbial survivability data, the authors find substantial lunar polar areas likely have surface conditions amenable to microbial survival.
AI.conclusion: Lunar polar regions may be less hostile to microbial survival than previously assumed, though only in a cryptobiotic state (survival without growth). Since many examined microbes will likely be transported to the Moon during planned crewed south pole exploration missions, thoughtful exploration planning and impact tracking are essential to limit and understand potential unintended life transfer to the Moon.

title: BioKERN: Biological Kernel Regularization for Histology-to-Transcriptomics Neighborhood Retrieval
summary: Spatially resolved biology requires representations that preserve biological neighborhood structure rather than only exact cross-modal correspondences. Existing histology--transcriptomics objectives can emphasize instance-level matching even when non-paired spots share molecular or spatial context. We introduce BioKERN, a multimodal spatial representation-learning framework that incorporates biological structure as an explicit, learnable inductive bias. BioKERN constructs a training-time biological kernel by combining transcriptomic similarity and spatial proximity, then uses it to provide graded neighborhood supervision and regularize embedding geometry. Evaluation uses a fixed, model-independent biological neighborhood definition shared by all methods. Across Mouse Brain Visium and Human Liver GSE240429, BioKERN consistently improves biological-neighborhood retrieval over BLEEP in both single- and multi-scale settings. Controlled shared-architecture experiments show that most of the improvement arises from biological-kernel regularization rather than increased model capacity. These results support explicit biological geometry as an interpretable inductive bias for multimodal learning in spatial biology.

AI.tldr: BioKERN is a multimodal spatial representation-learning framework that incorporates explicit biological structure (transcriptomic similarity + spatial proximity) as a learnable inductive bias, improving biological-neighborhood retrieval over existing methods like BLEEP in mouse brain and human liver datasets.
AI.motivation: Existing histology-transcriptomics objectives emphasize instance-level matching even when non-paired spots share molecular or spatial context, failing to preserve biological neighborhood structure in learned representations.
AI.method: BioKERN constructs a training-time biological kernel combining transcriptomic similarity and spatial proximity, which provides graded neighborhood supervision and regularizes the embedding geometry.
AI.result: Across Mouse Brain Visium and Human Liver GSE240429, BioKERN consistently improves biological-neighborhood retrieval over BLEEP in single- and multi-scale settings, with controlled experiments showing most gains come from kernel regularization rather than model capacity.
AI.conclusion: Explicit biological geometry serves as an interpretable inductive bias for multimodal learning in spatial biology.
